title: Encrypted Remote Manifest
description: The single encrypted manifest/index object that serializes multi-device synchronization. Committed via a conditional write (If-Match / versioned If-Match). After decryption it lists the current set of remote objects with their version lineage so devices can compare without listing. The manifest itself is encrypted as an object (see encrypted-envelope.schema.json); this schema describes the decrypted manifest payload. Schema version 1. The manifest carries only opaque object names + sizes/times (FR-160b accepted observable-leakage bound); semantic object types are encrypted inside each object, NOT exposed here. Assets appear as independent entries (FR-090a) — never bundled inside note envelopes.

manifestVersion.description: Opaque version token used as the If-Match precondition (e.g. an opaque tag or numeric version). Changing entries changes this token.

entries.description: One entry per remote object (note, asset, tombstone). Object names are opaque; semantic type is encrypted inside the object, NOT exposed here.

objectName.description: Opaque remote object name (random). The provider sees this name; it reveals nothing semantic.

objectId.description: Opaque object id matching the envelope's objectId (used as AAD). Not the semantic entity UUID.

contentHash.description: SHA-256 of the decrypted canonical object bytes (envelope integrity / dedup).

tombstones.description: Tombstones tracked at the manifest level so a returning device can reconcile deletion history before uploading. Each points to a deleted note lineage.
